Another efficient ingot-production practice has also become more common: increasing the silicon mass within the ingot crucible by adding fluidized bed reactor (FBR) polysilicon pellets, which fill voids between Siemens polysilicon chunks. The resulting higher charge weight helps lower the total cost of ownership for manufacturers by producing a greater ingot mass from each loading cycle. 2.5.2 Domestic Production of Ingots and Wafers Figure 19 reports PV wafer capacity and production in the United States between 2013 and 2024. The inset shows capacity with financing secured and under construction as of Q2 2025, organized by location of company headquarters.20 While no ingot and wafer production appears from 2015 through 2024, some U.S.-headquartered wafer interests—including startup and R&D- focused CubicPV and equipment supplier Applied Materials—existed during that time. A history of U.S. manufacturing during 2013–2020 is available (Basore and Feldman 2022b). 20 The location of company or parent company headquarters is organized as “U.S. HQ,” “China HQ,” or “Other HQ” according to the headquarters identified on the website of each company or parent company. The organization is not based on where each company acquired the underlying IP and licensing agreements for their process, whether they acquired any assets from a company headquartered in a different country, whether most of the company’s operations are in a different country from the headquarters of record, or the nationalities of the company’s owners. 27 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. The ingot and wafer 45X MPTC became available in 2022, and Corning and Qcells began constructing facilities in 2024.21 Based on BNEF data, industry interviews, and publicly available data, of the 10 GW of NLR-estimated domestic ingot and wafer capacity under dc construction as of Q2 2025, 5 GW could come online by the end of 2025, reaching 10 GW in dc dc 2026.22 We estimate there is a high probability that ingot and wafer production will constitute the largest gap between U.S. PV supply and demand for at least two more years. The scheduled 45X MPTC and domestic content bonus credit criteria help make the case for U.S. domestic wafer manufacturing, but they are less supportive than incentives for solar cells (U.S. Internal Revenue Service 2025b). Moreover, CapEx for ingot and wafer facilities that could come online in 2025 is not expected to be paid off before the scheduled end of the 45X MPTC and domestic content bonus credit. Figure 19.
